LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Poetry 2.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Types of poems: - Concrete - Ac, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 2.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Types of poems: - Concrete - Ac.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 2.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Types of poems: - Concrete - Ac.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 2.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Types of poems: - Concrete - Ac.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 2.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Types of poems: - Concrete - Ac.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. went

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

5. When practising Non- Fiction: Biography -Features -Functions -Examples, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   C. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 1.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Stanzas: - Couplet- 2 lines - T.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Types of Poetry: Form and Structure Stanzas: - Couplet- 2 lines - T.

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

8. When practising Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature -Traditional sources of or, which approach is best? (1 mark)

----
